label: the nine headword characters without a direct script-lesson owner
note: RE-DERIVED FROM DIRECT OWNERS, NOT ESTIMATED. 69 distinct Malayalam characters appear in headwords across 472 lessons; 60 occur in the headword of a writing/script lesson and nine do not -- 87 per cent direct-owner closure. ML-S148-letter-pha adds both the new headword character ഫ and its direct owner, so the open set is unchanged. Counts below are headword FIELDS first and distinct TOKENS second, so repeated sibling headwords are visible instead of silently collapsed: ള ḷa U+0D33 (24 fields / 19 tokens), ശ śa U+0D36 (17 / 13), ങ ṅa U+0D19 (14 / 12), ർ chillu-r U+0D7C (11 / 11), ധ dha U+0D27 (7 / 6), ൈ ai sign U+0D48 (5 / 5), ബ ba U+0D2C (4 / 4), ഖ kha U+0D16 (3 / 3), ഛ cha U+0D1B (2 / 2). This is deliberately a DIRECT-OWNER measure: the broader script-closure gate can credit glyphs appearing inside a writing lesson's examples, so calling these nine 'never taught' would conflict with that metric. The old 'sha (14)' mixed an ambiguous English name with an unrecoverable count; U+0D36 is open, while U+0D37 ഷ is directly owned by ML-S121-letter-ssa.
